item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: A triangle on top of a rectangle]

The figure above is made from a rectangle and a triangle with three equal sides.
What is the length, in centimeters, of side AB ?
item.figure_description: A composite figure composed of a rectangle at the bottom and a triangle on top sharing the rectangle's top edge as its base. The rectangle's bottom horizontal side is labeled "8 cm", and its right vertical side is labeled "3 cm". The triangle's top vertex is labeled A, and its bottom-right vertex (which is also the top-right corner of the rectangle) is labeled B.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three triangles labeled 3, 4, 5 on the left side ordered from top to bottom and each with a line arrow labeled Steve’s Rule pointing to the right at a square shaped box labeled 8, 10, 12 from top to bottom.]

Steve used a rule to get the number in the □ from the number in the △.
What was the rule?
reference_items.figure_description:
Three horizontal rows showing input and output shapes connected by an arrow. In each row, there is an upright triangle on the left, an arrow pointing to the right with the text "Steve's Rule" centered above it, and a square on the right containing a number:
- Top row: Triangle with the number 3 inside, pointing to a square with the number 8 inside.
- Middle row: Triangle with the number 4 inside, pointing to a square with the number 10 inside.
- Bottom row: Triangle with the number 5 inside, pointing to a square with the number 12 inside.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a piece of string curved both ends and a rule in cm with value from 1 to 10.]

If the string in the diagram above is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description:
A metric ruler and a folded piece of string above it. The ruler has major tick marks labeled from 1 to 10 with "cm" before the 1, and intermediate half-centimeter tick marks between each number.

The string is laid horizontally above the ruler with both ends folded back:
- The bottom-left end starts at the 4 cm mark and extends left to the 3 cm mark, where it loops around 180 degrees.
- The middle section runs continuously to the right from the 3 cm mark to approximately the 8 cm mark.
- At approximately the 8 cm mark, it loops around 180 degrees upward and extends back to the left, ending at approximately the 6.5 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: six pieces of cardboard with length of the sides labeled in cm. Two of the pieces are square shaped with each side measured at 1 cm. Four of the pieces are rectangular shaped with two sides measured at 1 cm and two other sides measured at 2 cm.]

Susan has the 6 pieces of cardboard shown above. Which of the following shapes could Susan make using all 6 of these pieces without cutting them?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, six gray-shaded flat cardboard shapes are shown. Two are identical squares, each labeled '1 cm' on all four sides (top, bottom, left, and right). Four are identical horizontal rectangles, each labeled '2 cm' on the top and bottom sides and '1 cm' on the left and right sides.

The response options show line drawings of four 3D geometric solids with dashed lines representing hidden edges:
- Option A: A cube.
- Option B: A triangular prism resting on one of its rectangular faces.
- Option C: A truncated pyramid with a square or rectangular base and top.
- Option D: A tall right rectangular prism standing on a square base.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
A grid of 9 columns and 5 rows of 1 cm by 1 cm squares containing a shaded polygon. Outside the bottom-right corner of the grid, dimension arrows indicate that a single square is 1 cm wide and 1 cm high.

Defining grid coordinates from the top-left corner (0, 0) to the bottom-right corner (9, 5):
- The shaded polygon has vertices at (3, 1), (5, 1), (6, 2), (5, 3), (5, 4), and (3, 4).
- The left side is a vertical line from (3, 1) down to (3, 4), spanning 3 units.
- The bottom side runs horizontally from (3, 4) to (5, 4), spanning 2 units.
- The right side goes vertically up from (5, 4) to (5, 3), 1 unit.
- From (5, 3), a diagonal side goes up and to the right to grid intersection (6, 2).
- From (6, 2), a diagonal side goes up and to the left to grid intersection (5, 1).
- The top side runs horizontally from (5, 1) left to (3, 1), spanning 2 units.

reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled A, B, C, and D, each partitioned into 4 regions:
- Option A: Divided into 4 equal quadrants by a vertical line and a horizontal line through the center.
- Option B: Divided into two squares by a central vertical line, with each square bisected by a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 4 identical right-angled triangles.
- Option C: Divided into 4 equal horizontal bands by three evenly spaced horizontal lines.
- Option D: Divided into 4 unequal regions by three parallel diagonal lines sloping up and to the right, creating two corner triangles and two trapezoids of unequal sizes.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
